name: Archgen Labs
long_description:
Archgen Labs builds AI-powered chip design tools for the next generation of 3D semiconductors.

Stacking compute vertically shortens connections and reduces the energy and delay of moving data. But it also makes heat harder to remove. Our tools help engineers optimize placement, timing, and temperature together so they can build faster, more power-efficient 3D chips.

Our GPU-accelerated placement engine ranked first in the Hudson River Trading macro-placement challenge. LayerTherm, our thermal analysis tool, predicts chip temperatures roughly 5,000× faster than conventional simulation in our benchmarks, helping engineers explore more designs and identify hotspots earlier. Newton, our AI chip design engineer, automates work across placement, routing, design-rule fixes, and timing closure.

We’re working with GlobalFoundries on 3D chip development, targeting our first tapeout in 2027.

launches.body:
**TLDR; We’re building the tools to out more transistors on a chip. Our foundational models run roughly 5,000× faster than current EDA software and our core placement engine ranked is #1 globally in Hudson River Trading’s macro-placement challenge.**\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=39z8-MXMiOI>

Hey everyone! We’re[ Hariharan Ayappane](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hariharan-ayappane/) and[ Naveen Venkat](https://www.linkedin.com/in/naveenvenkat17/), the founders of[ ArchGen Labs (YC F26)](https://archgenlabs.com/).

### **Chips of the future will be 3D**

For decades, better chips came from making transistors smaller. That’s getting harder and more expensive, while AI keeps demanding more compute within the same power and cooling budgets.

Part of the problem is distance. Moving data between components takes time and energy. Stacking computation vertically, like floors in a skyscraper, can bring those components closer together.

But shorter connections come with a trade-off: more computation in the same space makes heat harder to remove.

Engineers need to optimize placement, timing, and temperature together. Every change needs feedback. When those checks take too long, teams explore fewer designs.

We accelerate that loop.

### **What we’re building**

**1. Ultrafast foundational models for chip design**

LayerTherm uses physics-informed neural networks to predict a chip’s temperature map from its power distribution.

In our benchmarks, predictions averaged **62 milliseconds versus 314 seconds** for EDA solvers - roughly **5,000× faster**.

That lets engineers screen more candidate designs for hotspots before detailed thermal verification.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125553&key=user_uploads/3342660/3312c464-8b5c-4a0e-8cb4-5a2f64dd0de4)

**2. Worlds best chip design engine**

Our GPU-accelerated tools help engineers decide which components belong on each layer, shorten critical connections, and evaluate timing and thermal trade-offs.

The core placement engine ranked #1 globally in Hudson River Trading’s macro-placement challenge:[ https://archgenlabs.com/blog/posts/how-we-ranked-first-in-the-partcl.html](https://archgenlabs.com/blog/posts/how-we-ranked-first-in-the-partcl.html)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125553&key=user_uploads/3342660/6e1de1c7-ae47-4834-a974-8c54ba0b3474)

**3. Fully autonomous AI chip design engineer**

Newton works through placement, routing, design-rule violations, and timing repairs. It tests candidate changes, rejects weak ones before expensive checks, and carries forward verified results.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125553&key=user_uploads/3342660/6fd919cb-a7fd-49a0-85be-dcce33a92b02)

### **Where we are**

We’ve signed pilot projects and are working with GlobalFoundries to build 3D chips. We’re targeting our first tapeout in mid-2027.

### **Our ask**

We’d love to meet:

* Physical-design and timing teams facing a difficult closure problem or an upcoming tapeout.
* AI accelerator and 3D IC teams working through power, interconnect, or thermal constraints.
* Foundry and advanced-packaging engineers interested in evaluating tools for stacked logic.

If that sounds like your team, tell us where your design process gets stuck. We’d love to explore it with you.

Reach us at [founders@archgen.tech](mailto:founders@archgen.tech)
